title: Building Web APIs in ASP.NET Core

cards.title: Introduction to Web API
cards.content:
ASP.NET Core Web API is a framework for building HTTP services that can reach a broad range of clients, including browsers and mobile devices.

It is built on top of ASP.NET Core and relies on controllers that inherit from ControllerBase.

cards.title: Routing and Attributes
cards.content:
Web APIs use attribute routing to define endpoints. The [ApiController] attribute enables-opinionated, API-specific behaviors.

[Route("api/[controller]")]
[ApiController]
public class ProductsController : ControllerBase
{
    // Actions go here
}

cards.title: Return Types and IActionResult
cards.content:
Web API action methods can return specific types, IActionResult, or ActionResult.

Using ActionResult allows you to return either a type T or an HTTP status code response (like BadRequest() or NotFound()).

[HttpGet("{id}")]
public ActionResult GetProduct(int id)
{
    var product = _repository.GetById(id);
    if (product == null) return NotFound();
    return product;
}

cards.title: Dependency Injection in Web API
cards.content:
ASP.NET Core has built-in support for Dependency Injection (DI). Services are registered in Program.cs and injected into controller constructors.

private readonly IProductRepository _repository;

public ProductsController(IProductRepository repository)
{
    _repository = repository;
}

cards.title: Summary of Web API Fundamentals
cards.content:
You have learned the core concepts of ASP.NET Core Web API:

  • Using ControllerBase and [ApiController]
  • Mapping HTTP verbs (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)
  • Handling routes and status codes via ActionResult
  • Applying Dependency Injection for services
